page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.e4.xlarge is an x86_64 architecture server instance powered by an Intel Xeon E5-2682 v4 processor running at 2.5 GHz. This instance features 4 vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores with a shared CPU allocation model and 1.0 thread per core. It is configured with 32.0 GB of system memory, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per core, and includes a 40 MB L3 cache. The instance does not include local storage or complimentary public IPv4 addresses, and it operates on a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps under a KVM hypervisor.

Benchmark data indicates that this instance delivers entry-level performance across compute and memory operations. The stress-ng single-core CPU performance score of 950.58 falls within the bottom 10%, while the multi-core score of 3679.45 is in the bottom 25%. Memory bandwidth tests show 321.53 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 30.12 GB/sec for uncached large blocks, both placing in the bottom 25%. Similarly, the PassMark CPU score of 5065.1 and memory score of 1577.49 reflect lower-tier processing speeds.

The shared CPU allocation model and older Intel Xeon architecture present a clear tradeoff, resulting in lower computational throughput as evidenced by the poor multi-threaded bzip3 decompression speed of 13.51 GB/sec and a 135M LLM prompt processing speed of 167.69 tokens/sec. However, the 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio offers a high memory density relative to the processing cores. This configuration is qualitatively cost-efficient for memory-bound workloads that do not require intense CPU performance, such as basic Redis caching (achieving 5.32 million SET operations per second), lightweight database operations, and static web serving.
